data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel is *less* reliable because the 'checklist' introduces a new failure mode: 'semantic drift', where non-experts misinterpret the checklist's requirements in a way that an expert would never do.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist items are strictly binary and visually/physically verifiable (e.g., 'Is the red light on?').","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel includes a 'moderator' who ensures semantic alignment of the checklist terms.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition is a holistic integration of domain knowledge. A checklist decomposes this into discrete steps. Non-experts, lacking the holistic context, may satisfy the 'letter' of a checklist item while violating its 'spirit' (e.g., checking 'Is the valve closed?' as 'Yes' because the handle is turned, despite the valve being sheared off internally). The 'reliability' of the checklist is an illusion based on the assumption that the checklist items are unambiguous.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
